title: Apple Cinnamon Steel-Cut Oatmeal
changes_from_base: Steel-cut oats are soaked overnight in just-boiled water, so in the morning they need only a few minutes on the hob instead of the long simmer; they finish in cloudy apple juice and milk with grated apple, dark brown sugar and cinnamon, topped with toasted walnuts.
summary: Wholesome steel-cut oats enriched with fresh apple and juice, with the gentle warmth of cinnamon and the satisfying crunch of toasted walnuts.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
eating apple, peeled and coarsely grated (about 60 g)

steps.title: Soak overnight
steps.text: The night before, boil 720 ml water in a large saucepan, then take it off the heat and stir in 175 g steel-cut oats and ½ tsp salt; put the lid on and leave at room temperature until morning.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: The next morning, grate 1 peeled eating apple to get about 60 g.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Toast 60 g walnuts in a small dry pan 3-4 min, then chop and set aside.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Stir grated apple, 120 ml apple juice, 120 ml milk, 25 g dark brown sugar and ½ tsp cinnamon into the oats.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Bring to the boil over medium-high heat, then cook over medium 4-6 min, stirring now and then, until soft but chewy and like loose pudding.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Remove from heat, rest 5 min, then top each bowl with chopped walnuts.

tips: Soaking steel-cut oats overnight reduces cooking time and makes them creamier.
Use a box grater for quick, consistent apple shreds.
Toast walnuts while the porridge finishes cooking for fresh, aromatic nuts.
storage: Serve warm immediately; any leftover keeps chilled for 2 days and reheats gently with a splash of milk or juice. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
